description: Two Euclidean tracks of the one length, one driving a drum envelope with an accent envelope beside it, the other driving hats that do not start until the accent has fired

params.text: Sets how many steps both patterns run for, 1 to 32
Sets what share of the pattern's steps the drum fires on, 0% to 100%
Chooses which of every four clocks fires the accent envelope, counting from 1 to 7 round the four
Sets how long the accent envelope takes to fall, 10ms to 2 seconds
Sets how long the drum's envelope takes to fall, 10ms to 2 seconds; its FM envelope falls in half that
Bends the fall of the drum's FM envelope: at the bottom of its travel it collapses almost at once, at the top it falls close to a straight line
Sets what share of the pattern's steps the hats fire on, 0% to 100%
Divides or multiplies the hats clock, from a quarter of the incoming rate through it to four times it
Sets how long the hats envelope takes to fall, 5ms to 1 second
Bends the fall of the hats envelope: at the bottom of its travel it collapses almost at once, at the top it falls close to a straight line
Holds the hats back by that many clocks after the accent first fires, 1 to 4; moving it puts the hats back to not yet started

inputs.text: Each rising edge through 2V advances both tracks; the gap between edges is the tempo the hats divider works from, and every thirty-second edge puts both tracks back to their first step
Added to the drum's DECAY knob, a tenth of a second per volt; the total is held between 10ms and 2 seconds
Added to the hats DECAY knob, a twentieth of a second per volt; the total is held between 5ms and 1 second

outputs.text: The accent envelope, 0V to 10V, falling in the time set by A.DEC

notes: nothing steps and no envelope fires until a clock reaches CLK.
the hats stay silent until the accent envelope has fired once and the number of clocks set by SHIFT has gone by after it.

inputs.0:
high above 2V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.2:
continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
inputs.4:
continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
